Agent guide | Step 1 of 9

Start with the controller ready

Use an installed HTTPS controller and sign in as Admin or Super Admin. Ask the server team to confirm each server is RHEL 8/9 or Ubuntu 26.04, with systemd and sudo/root access.

Ask which CPU package to use: x86_64 = AMD64; aarch64 = ARM64. The same CPU binary supports both Linux families. The agent binary needs no separate Go, Python or Git setup; firewalld uses its normal OS packages.

Agents need outbound access to the approved control 8788 and discovery 8789 origins. There is no inbound agent management port.

Agent guide | Step 2 of 9

Create one reusable fleet setup

Click Install agent. Choose Fleet setup · reusable, enter a profile name and choose how long new enrollment is allowed.

Choose the matching Linux family and CPU architecture. The release team provides the agent package; the GUI download button supplies only the private setup file. Do not generate 20 different agents.

A fleet setup can be reused until it expires or is revoked. There is no fixed enrollment-count limit.

Agent guide | Step 3 of 9

Enter the correct controller addresses

For a direct default-port installation, use the same trusted name with these ports. The three addresses have different jobs:

Management / Control / Discovery, in that order
https://YOUR-CONTROLLER-NAME:8787
https://YOUR-CONTROLLER-NAME:8788
https://YOUR-CONTROLLER-NAME:8789

Use your actual LB URLs if they differ. Add the approved public HTTPS CA chain when required. Never upload a private key in the agent CA field.

Agent guide | Step 4 of 9

Choose preparation and download

Keep Control polling = 30 and Full inventory fallback = 900. Select Install missing OS dependencies only if your server team approves package installation. Otherwise, they must already provide firewalld, iproute/iproute2, ca-certificates and util-linux.

If Ubuntu uses UFW, optionally select Assess UFW and export migration data. UFW stays active. Installing missing firewalld packages does not start it or switch firewall managers.

Click Download private setup file. Keep prthak-agent-setup.json private. New installs stay monitor-only; installation does not authorize firewall changes.

Agent guide | Step 5 of 9

Copy the two items to each server

Ask your release/server team for prthak-agent-0.16.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz or prthak-agent-0.16.0-linux-arm64.tar.gz. They must verify the signature with approved independent trust and extract the matching package into a protected root-owned release folder on each server.

Copy the same private setup to /root/prthak-agent-setup.json, owned by root with permission 0600 (0400 is also accepted). The server team can set this in the transfer tool.

Do not copy another server's existing agent credentials or state. Your deployment tool can repeat the transfer and installation across all 20 hosts.

Agent guide | Step 6 of 9

Run one matching installer

RHEL 8 or 9
sudo ./scripts/install-agent-rhel.sh \
  --setup-file /root/prthak-agent-setup.json
Ubuntu 26.04
sudo ./scripts/install-agent-ubuntu.sh \
  --setup-file /root/prthak-agent-setup.json

Choose one command for that server. Wait for the result. The installer starts the seg-agent systemd service; it does not start firewalld or disable UFW.

A successful file install can still be waiting for the first report. Check the dashboard before calling the endpoint connected.

Agent guide | Step 7 of 9

Find the server and its services

Click Servers. Search for the hostname or its reported IP. Check a fresh heartbeat, correct OS and discovered service ports. Open its row for Services & health and Discovered services.

Example: SSH can be recognised on 2022 from the running process. The agent reports its interface IPs even when the controller connection crosses NAT.

New listener checks run every 5 seconds on supported native agents; full inventory normally refreshes every 15 minutes. A missing heartbeat raises an offline alert.

Agent guide | Step 8 of 9

Assign the location and tags

In Locations, create each real DC/cloud location. In Servers, select one or more hosts and click Assign tags & location. A host has one location and many tags.

For automatic assignment, add a subnet mapping. A /24 can override a larger /16. The same exact network cannot be allocated to two locations. Manual assignments remain in control.

You can also use Import CSV. Business tags and DCs are managed in the dashboard, not sent by the agent.

Agent guide | Step 9 of 9

Start safely and know what to check

First check inventory in monitor-only mode. Seeing a server does not mean firewalld enforcement is enabled. Use the reviewed configuration workflow before live policy changes.

Missing server? Ask the server team to check setup-file ownership, expiry, clocks, trusted CA and the exact 8788/8789 URLs. Keep an existing firewall manager running while the issue is reviewed.

No traffic history? Enable temporary learning or optional per-port monitoring separately. Neither is collecting by default. Agent CPU/memory depends on the workload; profile it during the pilot.

Native RHEL/Ubuntu firewall, rollback and DC testing remain to be performed in your environment.
